question: Sohan Singh Bhakna and Har Dayal were primarily associated with which of the following organisations?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ghadar Party**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**__**Ghadar Party**__:

__
 
• It was formed in 1913.
 
• Headquarters was at Yugantar Ashram in San Francisco.
 
• It was founded by Sohan Singh Bhakna and Lala Hardayal.
 
• The Ghadar Party was organized by migrants Indians in the United States.
 
• The old name of the Ghadar Party was the Pacific coast Hindustan association.
 
• The name Ghadar party was adopted after the launch of its journal Ghadar in 1913.
 
• It was formally dissolved in 1948.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 Kisan Sabha
 Also known as the All India Kisan Sabha, it was an organization meant to address the issues and rights of peasants (kisan means peasant).
 Established in 1936 in Lucknow at the All India Kisan Congress session.
 Swami Sahajanand Saraswati, N.G. Ranga, and Baba Sohan Singh Bhakna.
 Address farmers' issues like debt, land tenure, tenancy, rents, etc.
 
 

 Anushilan Samiti
 Anushilan Samiti was a revolutionary group in Bengal primarily working towards India's independence from British rule. The group carried out a number of violent operations against the British.
 Established in 1902 in Calcutta.
 Barindra Kumar Ghosh and Bhupendranath Dutta.
 Aimed at overthrowing British colonial rule in India through revolutionary means.
 
 

 Yugantar
 Yugantar was one of the prominent revolutionary organizations that were active in the fight for India's independence. The group also published a newspaper named 'Yugantar'.
 Founded in April 1906 in Calcutta.
 Barindra Kumar Ghosh, Bhupendranath Dutta, and Abhinash Bhattacharya
 The organization aimed to secure independence from British rule using more aggressive means, including armed revolution. The Yugantar newspaper propagated these revolutionary ideas.
